FOR AGENTS

Live translation by the caller's language: a call menu can ask the caller which language they speak. The call then goes to agents who speak it first, and when the agent does not, the desk shows each line both ways: what the caller said in your language, with the original underneath. You can type a reply and see it in theirs. Where your organisation switches it on, the translation is also spoken: the caller hears you in their language, and you can stop the speaking at any time and keep the captions.

Verified callers: the Caller check panel shows how a caller proved who they are: a PIN or ID digits in the call menu, a one-time code you sent, or their voice. Calls and chats show Verified, and some actions wait until the caller is.

Recognised by their voice: callers who agreed are recognised by their voice while they talk to you. The panel says Voice matches, Voice does not match, or Possible recording; if they ask you to stop, one click deletes their voiceprint.

Ticket fields and macros: tickets show your organisation's own fields (an order number, a device, a branch) in a Ticket fields card. Macros do several things in one click: a reply, a note, the status and the tags.

Replies stay with you: a customer's reply, or a colleague of theirs who was on the email, now joins the ticket it answers, and a reply that reopens your ticket waits ten minutes for you before anyone else is offered it.

Telegram and Viber: conversations from your organisation's Telegram and Viber bots arrive like any other message. You can send a customer a start link, and start a message to someone who follows the bot, within each network's rules.

Help in your language: the help guides, Ask in Help and the Academy are shown in your language as translations arrive, marked as machine translations, with the English original one click away.

FOR SUPERVISORS

Conversation analytics: every call and chat is read for why the customer got in touch, how they felt at the start and the end, how hard it was for them, whether it was resolved, which competitors they named and which must-say phrases were missed. Six new reports, each opening its conversations, a search across them all, and What changed on every figure.

Outcomes and reasons have their own menu section: dispositions, outcome groups, not-ready reasons and their groups.

The ticket list shows when each ticket was opened and last changed. A ticket transferred to a team now goes to that team's agents, whatever skills its old queue asked for.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS

Website chat, rebuilt: a new chat for your websites with your colours, logo and font, dark mode, Arabic right to left, invitations by page and time, your own pre-chat questions, an offline form that becomes a ticket, files, typing on both sides, a rating, the transcript by email, and conversations that carry on across pages and visits. Signed-in visitors can be recognised from your own website. Existing embed codes keep working. Set it up, with a live preview, under Web chat.

Ticket fields, rules and macros: add your own fields and choose which each category shows and which must be filled in before resolving; triggers that act as tickets change, automations that act after time has passed, and shared or personal macros. Try a trigger on recent tickets before switching it on.

Help centres per brand: a public help centre for each brand, in your colours and in ten languages, with your published articles, search, Was this helpful?, a request form built from your ticket fields, and customers signed in to see their own tickets.

Caller authentication: a Check the caller step in call flows (PIN or ID digits, with lockout), one-time codes by SMS, WhatsApp or email, and the actions that need a verified caller.

Voice biometrics: connect a Phonexia server, ask call"}
